name: Emerging-market stress
value: Lira ~50/$ record low; no EM default found
summary: Turkish lira near record low of 50 per dollar under managed depreciation; no major EM default or capital controls found
state: The Turkish lira traded near 50 per dollar on 3 Nov, a record low, as authorities allow a controlled depreciation and intervene to limit sharper falls; October inflation was 29.77% (Trading Economics). The move has been at a managed pace rather than a 10% monthly fall. Searches on 8 Nov found no major emerging economy that had defaulted, imposed capital controls or sought emergency IMF support.
for_you: Households and firms in Turkey bear the cost of a weaker lira through import prices. Travellers and companies with lira exposure see the exchange rate move steadily rather than abruptly.
rubric_hit: No major EM in acute distress found; lira at managed pace, below the 10% monthly fall Watch line

sources.title: Trading Economics — Turkish Lira Holds at Record Lows

why: Energy-importing and heavily indebted emerging economies crack first in oil shocks and strong-dollar periods, with knock-on defaults and unrest.
drivers: Oil and food import bills, dollar strength, FX reserves, debt maturities, IMF programmes.

rubric.alert: A sovereign default or capital controls in a major emerging economy, or several in crisis at once.
rubric.watch: A major emerging economy's currency falls more than 10% in a month, its reserves fall fast, or it seeks emergency IMF support.
rubric.normal: No major emerging economy in acute currency or debt distress.
